info.title: AppyRig
info.description:
Read-only live view of OpenRig agent teams across machines. Every verb reads the last snapshot each machine pushed to this hub; none sends anything to a seat. POST JSON-RPC 2.0 to /v1/rpc with header x-fli-principal (agent:<name>, cli or human[:surface]) and the hub session cookie or Authorization: Bearer <hub token>.

33 methods; 1 are human-only in whole or in part (`x-human-only`) and refused with `forbidden` for agent and cli principals.

Every error carries `data.failureMode` (the canonical name) beside the integer code.

methods.name: account.list
methods.summary: Claude accounts, each with the machines signed into it (read from every machine's last push, so a changed login moves a machine on the next push), its plan tier and where it came from, and the 5-hour and 7-day windows against their resets. monthly is always not-reported: no source carries one.

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: db.rows
methods.summary: Rows of one table of a machine's OpenRig database (~/.openrig/openrig.sqlite), read-only: its collector opens it read-only (query_only; immutable when OpenRig is stopped) and pushes each table's newest rows by rowid, at most 500 rows and 600 KB per table, every text cell redacted, and any column whose name looks secret (token, key, password, secret, credential) blanked. truncated / total vs held say when a table is cut. status 'pending' = no rows from that machine's collector for that table (older than v1.5, or not sent yet). Paged: offset, limit (max 100).

params.name: table
params.summary: table name, as db.schema lists it

schema.description: table name, as db.schema lists it

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: db.schema
methods.summary: The live shape of the OpenRig database on a machine: tables, columns (type, nullability, primary key), foreign keys, the OpenRig version it was read under, and what changed since the previous OpenRig version seen (baseline on the first). Read-only: names and types only, never a row. status: 'no-openrig' (no database on that machine), 'unreadable' (reason says why), 'no-data' (older collector).

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: feedback.add
methods.summary: File an in-app feedback note (a verdict, a region, a note, the view state and optionally a PNG screenshot) into AppyRig's own data/feedback/ store. The only write AppyRig makes: it never touches OpenRig, a seat or the queue. Human-only (an agent reads notes, it does not file them). The screenshot is base64 PNG, at most 3 MB decoded (downscale to 1600 px wide first); send it over POST /v1/feedback, whose body limit is 5 MB. dryRun validates and writes nothing.

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: feedback.get
methods.summary: One feedback note in full (everything the viewer sent plus what the server added), with the route to its screenshot (GET /v1/feedback/<id>/screenshot.png) and its folder on the hub's disk.

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: feedback.list
methods.summary: The feedback notes filed in the app, newest first (verdict, region, the note's first 200 characters, route, whether it has a screenshot). indexFile is the same list as a file on the hub's disk (data/feedback/index.jsonl), readable without this API; read one in full with feedback.get.

methods.name: health.findings
methods.summary: OpenRig's health findings (the detectors' pathologies, such as ceremony amplification or review carousels) per machine, with the coverage and policy that say what an empty list means. assessment is 'findings' (some exist), 'none-found' (the detectors that ran found none: read caveats before treating that as healthy) or 'unknown' (not readable). It is never 'healthy': caveats lists why an empty list may not be all-clear (diagnosis off so scheduled detectors do not run, partial or zero coverage, an unreadable policy). data also carries the context-pressure roll-up, the restore-readiness verdict and the daemon's version and event-loop lag. Not machine health (health.get) and not a place to change a detector.

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: health.get
methods.summary: Machine health as each machine's collector last sampled it: Claude processes, tmux sessions, terminal shells and terminal apps (with their memory), memory used and total, memory pressure, swap. Each reading is a value or 'unavailable' with a reason, never 0. status 'no-data' means that machine's collector predates health (it is not an error and not a clean bill of health). sampleAgeMs is the age of the readings now.

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: history.transitions
methods.summary: Queue transitions: every state change of every queue item, as each machine's OpenRig daemon retained it (who moved it, when, into which state, and the closure reason and target), newest first, in pages. Each collector holds the newest 1000 and the hub serves what it holds: machines[] says how many (held), how many the daemon had when read (retained), whether it was cut (truncated) and the earliest time held, so say 'from <date>', never 'all history'. Rows also carry the item's source, destination and summary when it is still in that machine's last queue snapshot. Filters: machine, qitemId, seat (the actor, or the item's sender or owner), rig (the part after @), state, closureReason, text (substring of id, actor, closure, state, summary, tags). Page with limit (max 200) and before = the previous nextCursor (a keyset of the last row, so rows added between pages never shift a page). Not the same as history.list, which is what API callers did.

methods.name: library.get
methods.summary: One library item in full from the index: the row library.list returns plus, for a skill, its file names and sizes. File text is not carried (the collector sends the index only). Refuses library-item-not-found when that machine's library holds no such item (or has not been read yet).

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: library.list
methods.summary: OpenRig's library as each machine's collector read it (read-only): specs (agent, rig, workflow), skills and context packs, with name, version, source, summary, where it lives on that machine, and group facts (workflow steps and roles, skill file count and bytes, pack token estimate). The index only: no file text. machines[] says per machine whether the library was read (ok), is not there yet (pending) or that OpenRig lacks it (unsupported), and counts[] is null for a list that could not be read, so an empty list is never 'none'. Built-ins are the same on every machine; compare machines by name+version+source. Filters: group, kind, text; limit (default 200, max 500).

methods.name: mission.file
methods.summary: One file a rig's MISSION.md points at (a spec source, listed by absolute path) or one in the qa/ or shots/ folder beside it, by absolute path. Only paths on the list the rig's collector pushed are ever served; the answer is a status, never a failure: 'ok' (text for .md/.html, base64 for .png/.jpg), 'missing' (listed, not on disk), 'refused' (not on the list, never read), 'too_large' (over 256 KB text or 2 MB image; no bytes), 'pending' (listed, bytes not arrived yet), 'no-data' (that machine's collector has sent no list: older, or not yet). machine is required: the same rig name can exist on two machines.

params.name: machine
params.summary: machine id, e.g. m4 (required: one rig name can exist on two machines)

schema.description: machine id, e.g. m4 (required: one rig name can exist on two machines)

params.name: path
params.summary: an absolute path named by that rig's MISSION.md or in its qa/ or shots/, or the rig-relative form 'qa/<name>.md' / 'shots/<name>.png' (never '..')

schema.description: an absolute path named by that rig's MISSION.md or in its qa/ or shots/, or the rig-relative form 'qa/<name>.md' / 'shots/<name>.png' (never '..')

methods.name: rig.files
methods.summary: The files of a rig that its collector found next to its rig.yaml (rig.yaml, MISSION.md, CULTURE.md, LEARNED*.md, brief.md, REPORT.md, DEBRIEF.md; the spec's folder and its mission folder), and in specFiles the files the rig.yaml itself names (culture_file, docs[], rig / pod / member startup files; ids like rig:guidance/role.md). Names and sizes only; read one with rig.file. status says why a list is empty: 'no-spec' (no rig.yaml found for it), 'no-data' (older collector), 'pending' (found, not received yet).

result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: rig.outputs
methods.summary: Run card R4, read-only: what a run produced that its handoffs name. commits: commit ids (7-10 hex with a digit and a letter, never part of a longer token such as a qitem id) in the rig's handoff summaries and messages; flistudio: FliStudio resource (r_) and gate (g_) ids, with a link only when a handoff carried one. Each names the newest handoff that mentions it, the words around it, and how many handoffs do. The rig's files (REPORT, DEBRIEF, LEARNED) are listed by rig.files.

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: rig.waiting
methods.summary: Run card R2, read-only: what a rig is waiting on David for that the queue list alone can't show. gates: FliStudio gate ids (g_ + 10 hex) in the rig's handoff messages whose newest mention still calls them open, each with the words around it and a link only when a handoff carried one. ssh: the machine's user@host from AppyRig config machines.<id>.ssh (null: not configured), for a copyable attach line. AppyRig never opens, answers or attaches to anything.

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: seat.detail
methods.summary: What one OpenRig seat is configured with, for the Agent page: its resolved spec (name, version, profile, hash), startup files (path, delivery hint, required, when it applies), startup actions (type, phase, the text it sends, redacted and cut), peers, the daemon's recovery notes, and installed resources. Read from the daemon's node record by that machine's collector, on a slow timer, and pushed only when it changed; the resume token and command (they hold the Claude session id), transcript path and event payloads are NOT carried anywhere. status: 'ok'; 'pending' (nothing from that machine's collector for this seat yet: older than v2, not sent yet, or the daemon read failed); 'unsupported' (that OpenRig has no node routes); 'seat-not-found' (the routes exist but the daemon does not know this seat); 'not-openrig' (a plain tmux seat has none).

result.name: result
result.description: The call envelope: `ok: true` with the value, or `ok: false` with a named refusal.

methods.name: seat.loadout
methods.summary: What one seat runs with, for the Debug view: the skills Claude Code listed to it (the newest full skill_listing in its transcript plus its later additions, counted once each; each sorted by source: role, repo, personal, plugin, builtin, or unplaced when the seat's folder is gone; same-named copies flagged) and its documents (culture, role, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, recap, learned), present or absent. Listed = available to the model; which skills were used is not reported. status: 'not-claude' (Codex and terminal seats are not read yet), 'no-listing' (no skill listing found), 'pending' (no loadout from this machine's collector for this seat: older than v1.5, or not sent yet).

methods.name: settings.get
methods.summary: The OpenRig daemon's configuration values per machine (read-only), from an allowlist of keys (daemon port and host, host name, transcripts on/off and sizes, health thresholds, snapshots, policies, retention, queue and feed and workflow tuning). Each setting carries its value, its source (default, env, file) and its default; changed is true when the source is not the default, so machines can be compared on what was set by hand. Path-like values are replaced by '(path hidden)' and withheld counts the keys never forwarded (paths, roots, anything secret-looking). Filter by key (exact, or a prefix ending in a dot) or changedOnly. Editing a setting is not available here.

params.summary: only this key, or this prefix ending in a dot

schema.description: only this key, or this prefix ending in a dot

params.summary: only settings whose source is not the default

methods.name: workflow.list
methods.summary: OpenRig workflows as each machine's collector read them (read-only): the workflow specs (name, version, purpose, target rig, terminal-turn rule, built-in) and the running or finished instances (id, workflow, status, current step, hops, times, deadline state). machines[] says per machine whether each list was read: specsRead / instancesRead true with an empty list means none exist (an instance list that is empty means no workflow has run); false means it could not be read, which is not the same. Instances can be filtered by status. Starting, routing or aborting a workflow is not available here.
